_meta.description: The three coverage sections the user asked to compare, verbatim from the request, plus the widest scope the project tracks. A 'section' is a definition of what counts as busy. Everything the site computes - the day board, the free windows, and the vacation analysis - is computed once per section so the three can be compared side by side.

tag_vocabulary.MLB: Any MLB game, all 30 clubs, Spring Training through the World Series. Giants and Athletics flagged high priority.
tag_vocabulary.NFL:49ers: San Francisco 49ers, preseason + regular season + postseason. High priority.
tag_vocabulary.NFL:national: Westwood One Sports national NFL radio broadcast (one game per window; not the whole NFL slate).
tag_vocabulary.NCAAF:California: California Golden Bears football. High priority.
tag_vocabulary.NCAAF:national: Westwood One Sports national NCAA football radio broadcast. NOT part of Sections 1-3 (the request lists Westwood One only for the NFL).
tag_vocabulary.MLS:Earthquakes: San Jose Earthquakes MLS. High priority.

section_ids.1: MLB (Giants + A's high priority, all 30 clubs) + NFL 49ers (preseason/regular/postseason, high priority) + Westwood One Sports national NFL radio.
section_ids.2: Section 1 + Stanford NCAAF and California NCAAF (high priority).
section_ids.3: Section 2 + San Jose Earthquakes MLS (high priority). This is the definition in the site's 'What free means' block.
section_ids.all: Every live over-the-air game this project tracks, including Westwood One national NCAA football. Shown for completeness; it is wider than any of the three sections.

_meta.why_not_every_nfl_game: The request lists only the San Francisco 49ers plus the Westwood One national feed for the NFL. Those two tags cover roughly five NFL dates a week (Sunday, plus the midweek national window), not all 272 games. The vacation analysis therefore ALSO blocks the NFL league calendar (Hall of Fame Game through the end of the season) as a conservative backstop - see scripts/analyze_vacation.py.
